claims.claim: Engine oil pump balance shaft assembly for Toyota cars like Toyota Camry (2018–present) and Toyota RAV4...
claims.evidence: Photos show an engine-related metal assembly, but no readable Toyota part number, engine code, or model-specific identifier to confirm compatibility with Camry 2018+ or RAV4.

risks.risk: Wrong part / wrong engine variant (balance shaft + oil pump assemblies differ by engine code and production year). Photos don’t show a readable part number or engine code.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the stamped/engraved part number label on the housing (or the exact Toyota OEM number) plus the engine code from the donor car (e.g., 2AR-FE/2GR-FE/others).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic used engine oil pump/balance shaft assembly with unknown compatibility (worst case: not matching the buyer’s engine).

risks.risk: Condition risk: internal wear, scoring, or bearing failure not visible in these angles; also possible oil leakage or damaged seals.
risks.proof: Video/close-ups of the bearing surfaces and shaft play (showing end float), and a photo of any seal faces; ideally a test/bench run or at least confirmation of smooth rotation.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as used and not guaranteed to be in perfect working condition (worst case: needs replacement/repair).

risks.risk: Missing components or incorrect kit contents (balance shaft assemblies may require specific gears, spacers, or bolts). Photos don’t confirm completeness.
risks.proof: Photo of everything included laid out (all gears/shafts/bolts/seals) and a checklist of what’s included vs what’s required for installation.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as incomplete/unknown kit contents (worst case: missing required parts).

risks.risk: Potential mismatch between seller’s description and actual item (could be a different pump/shaft assembly with similar housing).
risks.proof: Readable OEM part number from the housing (or a photo of the part number sticker/engraving) that can be cross-referenced.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not confirmed to be the stated oil pump balance shaft assembly.

proof_requests: Send a clear close-up photo of the exact OEM part number/stamp on the housing (no blur, taken straight-on).
Tell the donor car details: Toyota model, year, and engine code (or VIN last 6 digits) so compatibility can be verified.
Send a short video showing the shaft/bearing rotation smoothly and check for excessive play (end float).
Confirm what is included in the package (all gears/shafts/seals/bolts) with photos of the full set laid out.
response.reason: The photos show an engine-related metal assembly, but there is no readable part number or engine code to confirm it is the specific Toyota Camry (2018+) / RAV4 oil pump balance shaft assembly the seller claims. Without that, the correct price cannot be safely determined.
